numberBaseConverter.title: Number Base Converter
numberBaseConverter.subtitle: Binary · Octal · Decimal · Hexadecimal
numberBaseConverter.intro: Type a value with the keypad and read it back in another base. Only the digits that are legal in the source base stay enabled.

asciiConverter.title: ASCII Converter
asciiConverter.subtitle: Text ⇄ ASCII - BIN · OCT · DEC · HEX
asciiConverter.intro: Type on either side: the other one follows. The ASCII tab gives one 8-bit code per character; the Unicode tab shows the UTF-8 bytes of each character, up to 32 bits. Separators are optional — codes are read back in fixed-width groups.

modeHint.ascii: One byte per character, values 0–255. A character that needs more than 8 bits cannot be encoded here.
modeHint.unicode: UTF-8: 1 to 4 bytes per character (up to 32 bits). The bytes of one character are shown joined together.

errors.unrepresentable: "{{detail}}" needs more than 8 bits — switch to the Unicode tab.
errors.invalidDigit: "{{detail}}" is not a valid group in the selected base.
errors.outOfRange: "{{detail}}" is above 255, so it is not a byte.
errors.generic: The value could not be converted.

exercises.textToCodesUtf8: Write the UTF-8 codes of “{{text}}” in {{base}}.
exercises.codesToTextUtf8: Which text does the UTF-8 stream {{codes}} represent, written in {{base}} with no separators?

ipv4Calculator.title: IPv4 Calculator
ipv4Calculator.subtitle: Network · Broadcast · Mask · Subnets
ipv4Calculator.intro: Type an address and its mask to see the network it belongs to. Turn subnetting on to add bits to the host part and see how the network splits: the first and the last subnet are never assigned, and the table marks which ones are usable.
ipv4Calculator.noData: Type an address and a mask to see the calculation.
ipv4Calculator.firstSubnetReason: first subnet: it is the network address
ipv4Calculator.lastSubnetReason: last subnet: it is the broadcast address

errors.invalidIp: The address must have four octets between 0 and 255.
errors.invalidMask: The mask must be a whole number between 0 and 32.
errors.invalidSubmask: You can only add between 1 and {{max}} bits with this mask.
errors.generic: The network could not be calculated.

protocolBuilder.title: Build your Protocol
protocolBuilder.subtitle: Generic protocol header diagram · editable schema
protocolBuilder.intro: Add fields to the diagram with the green button, drag a type from the catalogue on the left onto a Free field, and set its length against the bit ruler. You are defining the header schema, not the values that travel in it.

empty.title: The diagram is empty
empty.hint: Use “Add field” to place the first Free field, then drag a type onto it from the catalogue.

add.singleHint: One Free field at the end of the diagram.
add.compositeHint: A named group, divided into two Free fields.
add.child: Add a field to the group

field.freeHint: Undefined field. Drag a type from the catalogue onto it, or double-click to define it.
field.noMeaning: No meaning written yet. Double-click the field to add it.

group.noMeaning: No meaning written yet. Use the pencil to add it.

palette.title: Field types
palette.hint: Drag a type onto a Free field, or select it and then click the field.

uint.label: Unsigned integer
uint.description: A plain binary number. You choose how many bits it takes: with n bits it covers 0 to 2ⁿ−1.

flag.label: Flag
flag.description: A single bit that is 0 or 1, like IPv4's DF. Its length is fixed at 1 bit.

enum.label: Enumeration
enum.description: A numeric code with one meaning per value, like IPv4's Protocol field (6 = TCP).

reserved.label: Reserved / padding
reserved.description: Unused bits, set to zero, kept to align the header or to leave room for future versions.

checksum.label: Checksum
checksum.description: The result of a computation over the rest of the header, used to detect transmission errors.

mac.label: MAC address
mac.description: The physical address of an interface. Its length is fixed at 48 bits.

ipv4.label: IPv4 address
ipv4.description: A network address in IPv4 form. Its length is fixed at 32 bits.

port.label: Port
port.description: Identifies the sending or receiving process. Its length is fixed at 16 bits.

values.label: Possible values
values.hint: One value per line, with the meaning the protocol gives it.

algorithm.label: Algorithm
algorithm.hint: Optional: how the checksum is computed.

form.description: A field is defined by what it means and by the bits it takes.
form.groupDescription: The group names the band and says what it means; each field inside is defined on its own.
form.name: Name
form.meaningPlaceholder: What this field carries and what it is for.
form.documentationHint: Where this field is described, if it comes from a standard.
form.groupMeaningPlaceholder: What this band of bits groups together.

errors.range: The length must be between {{min}} and {{max}} bits.

save.savedSession: Protocol saved for this session. Server persistence is not wired up yet, so it is lost when the page reloads.
save.error: The protocol could not be saved.
save.signedOut: Sign in to save your protocols.

share.title: Share the protocol
share.description: A read-only link to the saved protocol.
share.pending: The link is reserved: the public page goes live once server persistence is wired up.
share.needsSave: Save the protocol before sharing it: unsaved, there is nothing behind the link.
share.error: The link could not be generated.
share.signedOut: Sign in to share your protocols.

export.title: Export the protocol
export.description: The schema to open it again, or the diagram as a picture.
export.jsonHint: The whole protocol, ready to import back.
export.error: The file could not be generated.

clear.title: Clear the diagram?
clear.description: Every field and the protocol name are removed. If you have not saved it, it cannot be recovered.

fields.sourcePort: Port of the process sending the datagram.
fields.destinationPort: Port of the process meant to receive it.
fields.length: Total length in bytes of the header plus the data.
fields.checksum: Error check over the header and the data.

fields.dscp: Class of service requested for the packet.
fields.totalLength: Total packet length in bytes, header included.
fields.identification: Identifier grouping the fragments of one packet.
fields.moreFragments: Says more fragments follow this one.
fields.fragmentOffset: Where this fragment sits inside the original packet.
fields.ttl: Hops the packet has left before it is dropped.
fields.headerChecksum: Error check over the header only.

fields.destinationMac: Physical address of the interface meant to receive the frame.
fields.sourceMac: Physical address of the interface sending it.
fields.etherType: Upper-layer protocol carried in the frame.
